reason: This text (Exodus 1:15-22) emphasizes moral courage and fear of God, not rituals and ceremonies. The passage explicitly states that the midwives feared God and refused to obey Pharaoh's command to kill Hebrew infants. God rewarded them ('made them houses') specifically because they feared Him and preserved life—not because of any ritual observance. The entire narrative centers on ethical action (choosing to save lives) over political authority, demonstrating that what mattered to Yahweh in this context was moral faithfulness and reverence, not ceremonial practice. There is no mention of rituals or ceremonies anywhere in this passage.
